topology_reasoning.device: Grating-assisted contra-directional coupler (contra-DC). A straight central bus waveguide is flanked above and below by two corrugated (Bragg-grating) waveguides running parallel to it at a small coupling gap. Each grating waveguide loops back on itself through a 180-degree U-bend into a thick bar waveguide terminated in a sharp point taper (a reflection-suppressing termination), and connects to the outside world through a thin adiabatic S-curve lead (top-left for the upper arm, bottom-right for the lower arm - a 180-degree rotationally symmetric layout).
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: Light in the central bus phase-matches to the counter-propagating mode of the adjacent corrugated waveguide when the grating period satisfies the contra-directional phase-matching condition (period = lambda / (n_bus + n_grating_wg)). The corrugation provides the momentum kick; the drop signal exits backwards along the grating waveguide through the S-curve lead. The point-tapered bar sections radiate residual forward light so it cannot reflect back. Function-defining knobs: grating period (sets drop wavelength), corrugation duty cycle and tooth size (set coupling strength kappa and bandwidth), bus-to-grating gap (sets kappa), number of periods / coupling length (sets bandwidth and extinction), bus and grating waveguide widths (set the two effective indices and hence the phase-matching point).
topology_reasoning.calibration_note: Calibration is strongly anisotropic (200.05 px/um in x, 1620 px/um in y; device is physically 18.24 x 0.7 um and the figure is vertically stretched ~8x). All geometry below is designed in true um so that the absolute-scale renderer reproduces the target: x_um = (px-63)/200.0548, y_um = (1152-row)/1620.
